A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CI-CoT/CI-RL research. All 37 pages of each version, including Appendices A–G, are readable, and their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on synthetic contextual-integrity tasks and PrivacyLens, plus ConfAIde evaluations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including model comparisons, reward-weight ablations, and benchmark evaluations in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: The CI-CoT prompt, synthetic-data generation procedure, and GRPO-based CI-RL training with formatting and keyword rewards remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices B–C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic CI tasks, PrivacyLens, and ConfAIde tiers 1–4. No evaluated domain, population, or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical model and comparator membership, including the DeepSeek distilled reasoning models and CI-CoT/CI-RL comparisons in Tables 1–3. Appendix A comparisons also match.

E3.justification: The 590/66/73 training/validation/test split, checkpoint selection, model configurations, metrics, PrivacyLens judge settings, and Appendix F training settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The LLM-versus-LRM comparison, reward-weight ablation, training-generation example, PrivacyLens case studies, and output-length/correlation analyses are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Both checklists retain the statement that multiple runs and error bars were not completed. Appendix F retains the same output-length statistics and correlation analysis, with no new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 retain their entries and numerical values. For example, Qwen2.5-7B with CI-RL has 75.0% Integrity and 48.4% Complete in Table 1 in both versions. Qualitative examples and reported trends also match.

T1.justification: The GRPO objective, reward definitions in Equations 1–3, and metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty and effectiveness claims about CI reasoning, RL training, reduced disclosure, preserved utility, and transfer to PrivacyLens.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning synthetic data, coarse keyword rewards, model scaling, evolving norms, and generalization remain unchanged. Section 7.1 adds citations to an existing future-work statement without changing its meaning.

D1.justification: v2 refers generally to code and data in supplementary material. v3 adds explicit Hugging Face dataset and OpenReview code-supplement locations in Section 4 and updates checklist item 5 accordingly. Implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 7.1 adds Shi et al.'s work on multimodal parent-child interaction and Zeng et al.'s FutureSightDrive to the existing visual-reasoning discussion. These are limited citation additions; the broader positioning and Appendix G discussion remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 updates Reza Shokri's affiliation and email and revises resource-access wording in the checklist. The narrative, section organization, and appendix order are otherwise preserved.

P2.justification: Two new resource footnotes cause local reflow across pages 6–7, including shifted placement of Table 2. Added references reflow pages 12–13. Figure and table designs, captions, and contents are retained.

improvement.justification: Section 4 and checklist item 5 provide more actionable resource-access information than v2's general supplementary-material statement, improving discoverability and reproducibility documentation. The scientific content and appendix evidence remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited.
